Build a Markdown site for a source package

Source: R/build_site.R
build_site.Rd

Writes the reference, every R Markdown vignette and a front page as Markdown files that read as linked pages on github.com. The output has this layout:

  • README.md: the front page. It shows the package name, the version, the source commit when known, a list of articles and a link to the reference.

  • reference/: the output of build_reference().

  • articles/: one <name>.md file for each vignettes/*.Rmd file, with its figures in a folder beside it.

Usage

build_site(package = ".", output_dir, overwrite = TRUE)

Arguments

package

Path to a package source directory, which MUST contain a DESCRIPTION file. An installed package name is an error, because an installed package has no vignette sources.

output_dir

Target directory. Created if it does not exist.

overwrite

If TRUE (the default), build_site() deletes the README.md file and the reference/ and articles/ folders in output_dir before it writes the new set. If FALSE, it aborts when output_dir contains any file or folder.

Value

Invisibly, the path to output_dir.

Details

build_site() copies the whole vignettes/ folder to articles/, so images and other assets stay beside the articles. It renders each .Rmd file there with rmarkdown::github_document(html_preview = FALSE), in a new environment whose parent is the global environment. Then it deletes the copied .Rmd files and any .Rmd.orig files.

The front page lists each article under the title field of its YAML header, or under its file name when the header has no title. The commit comes from the GITHUB_SHA environment variable, else from git rev-parse HEAD in package. The front page shows its first 7 characters. When neither source gives a commit, the front page omits it.

Install the package before you call build_site() when a vignette calls library() on it. The vignettes run against the installed version, and the reference reads the source.

build_site() does not render Quarto (.qmd) vignettes. It copies them unrendered and gives a warning that names each one.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
csdocs::build_site(".", output_dir = "docs-build")
} # }
